newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan sees higher 1997 domestic output.
newsitem.headline: Nissan sees higher 1997 domestic output.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it expects its domestic vehicle production to rise 6.8 percent from a year earlier to 1.72 million vehicles in calendar 1997, after a projected 6.0 percent decline this year.
Japan's second biggest carmaker expects its domestic vehicle sales to rise 3.7 percent to 1.16 million vehicles in 1997, after a projected 0.3 percent increase in 1996.
The company also said that it expects its 1997 vehicle exports from Japan to rise 3.3 percent next year to 600,000, after a projected 2.9 percent drop this year.
It predicted its overseas production would rise 3.6 percent to 1.11 million next year, after projected flat growth in 1996.
It forecast overall domestic demand, excluding 660 cc mini-vehicles, would remain at 5.34 million vehicles in 1997 from the previous year.
